hints: Look at how properties change as you go down Group 2, both reactivity with acids and solubility of hydroxides follow the same direction.
Since L reacts more vigorously than N, L must be the more reactive metal and so it sits lower down the group than N.
Since M(OH)2 is more soluble than N(OH)2, M must also sit lower down than N, so N has to be the highest (least reactive) metal of the three.
walkthrough:
**Recall the reactivity trend in Group 2**

Great start, let's remember the big pattern. Reactivity increases down Group 2 because the outer electrons are lost more easily.

Trend: $\text{Ca} < \text{Sr} < \text{Ba}$ in reactivity with dilute acids

**Recall the hydroxide solubility trend**

Solubility of Group 2 hydroxides also increases down the group. So barium hydroxide is the most soluble and calcium hydroxide is the least soluble of these three.

Trend: $\text{Ca(OH)}_2 < \text{Sr(OH)}_2 < \text{Ba(OH)}_2$ in solubility

**Translate the two clues**

Clue 1: L reacts more vigorously than N, so L is below N in the group.

Clue 2: $\text{M(OH)}_2$ is more soluble than $\text{N(OH)}_2$, so M is also below N in the group.

**Identify N and check the options**

Both clues tell us N is above both L and M, so N must be the highest metal, calcium. Only the combination L = Ba, M = Sr, N = Ca fits both trends perfectly.

options.A: L = Ba is below N = Sr, so Ba reacting more vigorously than Sr is correct. However M = Ca is above N = Sr, so Ca(OH)2 would be less soluble than Sr(OH)2, which contradicts the statement that M(OH)2 is more soluble than N(OH)2.
options.B: L = Ba is below N = Ca, so Ba is more reactive than Ca and reacts more vigorously with dilute HCl. M = Sr is also below N = Ca, so Sr(OH)2 is more soluble than Ca(OH)2. Both statements are satisfied.
options.C: L = Ca is above N = Sr, so Ca would be less reactive and react less vigorously than Sr. This is the opposite of the first statement, even though M = Ba being below N = Sr correctly gives higher hydroxide solubility.
options.D: L = Sr is above N = Ba, so Sr would react less vigorously than Ba, contradicting clue 1. Also M = Ca is above N = Ba, so Ca(OH)2 would be less soluble than Ba(OH)2, contradicting clue 2.
